name: Indigenous peoples of Amazonia
summary: The peoples of the Amazon rainforest, who have lived there for over 11,000 years. Archaeology shows that some built large settlements, earthworks and fertile “dark earth” soils, larger and more complex than once believed.

knownFor.label: Terra preta
knownFor.note: Fertile “dark earth” made by people with charcoal and waste.

knownFor.label: Manioc (cassava)
knownFor.note: A root crop first domesticated in the southern Amazon.

knownFor.label: Marajoara pottery
knownFor.note: Painted pottery from Marajó Island at the mouth of the Amazon.

location.value: The Amazon basin: Brazil, Peru, Colombia, Ecuador, Bolivia, Venezuela and the Guianas.
location.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

terrain.value: Tropical rainforest with huge rivers and seasonally flooded forest.
terrain.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

climate.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

resources.value: Fish, turtles, game, fruit, nuts and forest plants; manioc gardens.
resources.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

disasters.value: Floods and droughts in some years.
disasters.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

population.value: Estimates for what is now Brazil around 1500 range from about 1 million to over 11 million; how many lived in the Amazon is strongly debated.
population.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples in Brazil (checked 9 Nov 2026)

urbanisation.value: Some large settlements: the Marajoara culture on Marajó Island (perhaps up to 100,000 people) and the Upper Xingu (13th–17th centuries, tens of thousands of people).
urbanisation.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples in Brazil (checked 9 Nov 2026)

disease.value: In the first 100 years after contact the population fell by about 90%, from disease made worse by slavery and violence.
disease.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples in Brazil (checked 9 Nov 2026)

migration.value: By 1500 Tupi-speaking peoples lived along almost the whole Atlantic coast of Brazil.
migration.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples in Brazil (checked 9 Nov 2026)

economicBase.value: Farming manioc and other crops in forest gardens; fishing and hunting.
economicBase.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples in Brazil (checked 9 Nov 2026)

tradeRoutes.value: River trade networks carried goods across the basin.
tradeRoutes.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

wealth.value: Wealth was counted in food, feathers and shared goods.
wealth.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

moneyAndTax.value: None; exchange was by gift and barter.
moneyAndTax.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

inequality.value: Varied: some groups were equal, others had chiefs and ranked lineages.
inequality.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

governmentType.value: No single state; villages and regional chiefdoms.
governmentType.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

keyRulers.value: No rulers were recorded in early times.
keyRulers.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

succession.value: Varied by people, often through kin lines.
succession.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

institutions.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

stability.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

eliteConflict.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

armyAndTech.value: Bows, blowguns with curare poison, clubs.
armyAndTech.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

majorWars.value: Resistance to Portuguese and Spanish slave raids.
majorWars.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

territoryChange.value: Lost land to colonists, rubber tappers and later ranchers.
territoryChange.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples in Brazil (checked 9 Nov 2026)

alliancesRivals.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

inventions.value: Curare poison, rubber (used for balls and waterproofing), hammocks.
inventions.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

scienceEducation.value: Knowledge of hundreds of medicinal plants.
scienceEducation.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

openness.value: Adopted metal tools from Europeans after contact.
openness.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

communicationTransport.value: Rivers were the highways: dugout canoes carried people and goods; in the Upper Xingu, roads and bridges linked large settlements.
communicationTransport.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples in Brazil (checked 9 Nov 2026)

religion.value: Animist beliefs, with shamans as healers and guides.
religion.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

languageWriting.value: Hundreds of languages (Tupi-Guarani, Arawak, Carib, Macro-Jê and others); Brazil’s 2022 census recorded 295 Indigenous languages.
languageWriting.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

artsArchitecture.value: Pottery (such as Marajoara ware), feather ornaments and body painting.
artsArchitecture.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples in Brazil (checked 9 Nov 2026)

socialStructure.value: Varied by people, from small villages to larger settlements.
socialStructure.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

sharedIdentity.value: Many separate peoples with their own languages.
sharedIdentity.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

dailyLife.value: Large communal houses (malocas) shared by several families, with hammocks; food from manioc gardens, fish, turtles, fruit and game.

neighbours.value: Andean peoples, and later the Portuguese and Spanish.
neighbours.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

ideasReligions.value: Jesuit missions, from the mid-16th century until the Jesuits were expelled in the 18th century.
ideasReligions.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples in Brazil (checked 9 Nov 2026)

colonisation.value: Colonised from the 16th century; the rubber boom (about 1879–1912) brought violence and the invasion of Indigenous lands.
colonisation.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

riseSignals.value: Managed forests and soils over thousands of years.
riseSignals.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta; Eos (AGU): Amazon resilience, 18 Dec 2025 (checked 15 Nov 2026) (Indigenous peoples have shaped the landscape for at least 13,000 years, with terra preta, planted forest areas and earthworks; the page does not cover the 500–1500 CE peak, post-1492 collapse or slave-raid resistance)

peakPeriod.value: Possibly around 500–1500 CE, when large settlements existed.
peakPeriod.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

declineSignals.value: Disease after 1500 and colonisation reduced many peoples.
declineSignals.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

outcome.value: Hundreds of peoples still live in the Amazon, including some with little outside contact (Brazil counted 67 uncontacted groups in 2007).
outcome.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples in Brazil (checked 9 Nov 2026)

sources.value: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples in Brazil; Terra preta; Heckenberger, The Ecology of Power (2005).
sources.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta

overallCertainty.value: Mostly known from archaeology; population size is strongly debated.
overallCertainty.source: Wikipedia: Indigenous peoples of the Americas; Wikipedia: Terra preta
